title: Network Engineer Roadmap
summary: Build from networking fundamentals and Linux into routing, switching, network security, automation, cloud networking and production infrastructure.

facts.Timeline assumption: Four-year B.Tech/B.E. beginning in 2026 and completing around 2030. Each semester should produce a practical networking skill or demonstrable lab.

about.label: Career fit
about.text: Network Engineer is a directly aligned career path for ECE;

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: build networking, Linux, routing, switching, troubleshooting and network-security fundamentals.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: specialise in enterprise networking, network security, cloud networking, wireless or network automation.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: progress toward senior network engineering, network architecture, cloud infrastructure or security engineering.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: combine networking with cloud, automation, software-defined networking, security and AI-assisted operations.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Move from manually configuring individual devices toward automated, software-defined and cloud-connected networks. Develop strong security, observability and infrastructure-as-code habits alongside traditional networking.

blocks.label: Career progression

blocks.text: PhD routes

Keep networking skills connected to cloud infrastructure, automation and security. Senior network professionals increasingly need to understand software-defined infrastructure, APIs, observability, hybrid/multi-cloud environments and automated operations in addition to traditional routing and switching.
